rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — search EDGAR for shelf filings (S-3), prospectus supplements, and Item 1.01 8-Ks filed BEFORE the 2025-05-15 cutoff that signal undisclosed dilution.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch the filings do not telegraph. A $110M ATM shelf is ~12% of the ~$907M public float (using YE2024 non-affiliate float per 10-K). For a 17.9M-share utility, that is meaningful overhead supply that the 10-K's 'Sources of Liquidity' section and Q1 10-Q materially under-emphasize. Filed 3 calendar days before the backtest cutoff — the timing means the equity supply is structurally present but not yet absorbed at pre-cutoff prices. Reads as 'we need balance-sheet capacity beyond DRIP for the $387M 2025-27 CapEx program' but the disclosure cadence (silent in 10-K and Q1 10-Q, then a $110M shelf with three underwriters on 11-day notice) is the kind of late-quarter capital action the framework flags.

Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01) does not affirmatively confirm a fully executed Settlement Agreement and does not disclose a dollar value, but reiterates the immateriality claim. Not provably underdelivering — but the implied claim ('immaterial') is not yet fully demonstrated in a hard number.

rfm_tuples.R: We expect to spend approximately $387 million for capital projects through 2027 ... we use internally generated funds, short-term and long-term debt borrowings, proceeds from sales of common stock under the Investment Plan and, when market conditions are favorable, proceeds from sales to the public of our common stock.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — cross-walk the $387M 2025-2027 CapEx plan vs current funding sources (operating cash flow $58.7M FY2024; $140M lines of credit with $23M drawn at YE24, $34M at 3/31/25; mortgage covenants restrict debt). Derive the implied external-capital ask.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $387M over 3 years = ~$129M/yr CapEx vs $58.7M FY2024 operating cash flow = $70M/yr funding gap. DRIP raised only ~$1.0M in FY2024. 2025-2027 maturity schedule on long-term debt is $7.7M / $7.5M / $7.3M — manageable. The 5/12/2025 $110M ATM shelf (claim C3) is sized exactly to close roughly one year of the funding gap. Q1 2025 net income $9.5M vs $10.7M prior-year Q1 (-11.5%), EPS $0.53 vs $0.60.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The CapEx-plan disclosure is honest in numerator ($387M is stated) but the 10-K narrative under-emphasizes the equity-issuance dependency. Operating cash flow covers ~45% of planned CapEx; DRIP supplies a rounding error; mortgage covenants cap incremental secured debt. The post-cutoff $110M ATM is exactly the math the 10-K should have telegraphed more loudly. Q1 2025 earnings decline (-11.5% YoY) reduces the internal-funding contribution further. Honest about the spend, soft on the cap-structure implication.

Net income $44.4M FY2024 vs $31.6M FY2023 — material rebound aided by 3M Settlement recoveries (carrying-cost component). But the implied earnings durability is softening: Q1 2025 EPS is down 11.5% YoY despite the full annualized tariff being in effect, suggesting cost pressure (interest expense from the climbing line-of-credit balance + non-recurring 3M-recovery tailwind tapering). Rate case is real and large; earnings translation is incrementally underwhelming.

rfm_tuples.R: We have paid dividends on our common stock each year since 1912 and have increased the amount of dividends paid each year since 1973. Our earnings, financial condition, capital requirements, applicable regulations and other factors ... will determine the amount of future dividends.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the dividend-aristocrat claim is sustainable given the funding gap (claim C6), the post-cutoff dilution (claim C3), and the Q1 2025 earnings decline (claim C9).
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2024 net income $44.4M on 17.89M diluted shares = $2.48 EPS; current quarterly dividend $0.33/sh = $1.32 annual = ~53% payout ratio on FY2024. On Q1 2025 annualized EPS of $2.12, payout ratio rises to ~62%. With $387M CapEx through 2027 and Q1 2025 financing cash flow already showing increased credit-line drawdown, dividend continuity is funded out of fresh equity/debt, not free cash flow. The 51-year consecutive-increase streak is honestly disclosed but operates as a constraint, not a buffer.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The historical dividend record is true; the forward sustainability is reasonable but structurally dependent on the ATM equity program disclosed 3 days before cutoff. This is honest disclosure with no claim drift — the company is not concealing the funding mechanics, just under-emphasizing the equity-issuance leg.

summary: MSEX is structurally honest disclosure with three Mode B catches that the 10-K narrative does not telegraph: (1) a $110M ATM equity shelf filed 3 days before cutoff that neither the 10-K nor the 5/1 Q1 10-Q hints at, sized at ~12% of public float; (2) an auditor swap (Baker Tilly dismissed, PwC appointed) executed days before the original 10-K filing, with the 10-K/A filed two weeks later to retrofit Baker Tilly's omitted signature — coupled with prior-year ICFR material weaknesses claimed-remediated but not yet re-audited; (3) the $387M 2025-2027 CapEx plan implies ~$70M/yr external funding gap, with zero insider buying through a -16.6% drawdown and Q1 2025 EPS already down 11.5% YoY. The dividend-aristocrat status and rate-case recovery are real, but earnings durability and dilution overhang are softer than the narrative suggests. NEUTRAL with a tilt toward SHORT — not a 'lying detector' fire, but the capital-action choreography is the framework's signature pattern.
